newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes firm, Brent CFDs see active trade.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes firm, Brent CFDs see active trade.

text.p: North Sea crudes stayed firm on Wednesday, supported by thin supply of February barrels and delays to Ekofisk loadings, but most activity was confined to short-term swaps, traders said.

Dated Brent was seen firming slightly to talk around Mar Brent +35 cents after trade on Tuesday at +30 cents as a U.S. refiner sought a million barrels for a mid-month requirement left uncovered by the Ekofisk delays, they added.
Problems commissioning a pipeline tie-in of the U.K. Fulmar field to Norway's Ekofisk stream was compounding week-long delays caused by a shutdown in January.
No new wet deals were reported but traders expected a Feb 19-21 Brent to find a buyer at the firmer levels later on.
Brent CFDs were actively traded, the balance of this week's dates fetching Mar Brent +31 cents four times and next week trading at Mar Brent +19 cents after a deal at +18 cents earlier in the day.
Feb 17-21 traded at Apr Brent +45 cents, dealers added.
Intermonth spreads were mixed with Mar/Apr holding onto early gains at +45/+48 cents and Feb/Mar slipping to talk around +47/+50 cents after an early bid at +55 cents disappeared.
Two Brents were due to turn wet on Wednesday, traders said.
West African markets were fairly quiet ahead of the release of the March loading programme for Nigerian crudes, expected later today or tomorrow, traders said.
"All eyes are on the March programme," said one.

Differentials were assessed fairly steady. An Angolan Cabinda/Nemba combination cargo loading Feb 26-28 traded on Wednesday at Dated Brent -70 cents for Cabinda and Dated Brent "plus a few cents" for Nemba.
This was in line with another Cabinda trade on Tuesday at Dated Brent -70 cents for a Feb 23-25 loader.
